13.0.s.en: (3) Keeping away from the worship of idols

13.0.2.en: A warning of a danger that could make Israel fall into disobedience, which is the appearance of a false prophet, or one who claims to be a man of visions and dreams, and his attempt to prove the truth of his claims by some miraculous deeds.

13.1.0.en: He forbids following the false prophet in turning away from God, even if his prophecy comes true or he works a dazzling miracle, for all this is a deception of Satan.

13.2.0.en: God permits these false claims of prophecies and dreams in order to test His people, whether they remain firm in faith in Him or leave Him, because the true believer in God does not let anything draw him away from Him, however great it may be. Magicians appeared in the Old Testament such as Jannes and Jambres in the days of Moses (2 Tim 3:8), and Simon and Bar-Jesus in the days of the Apostles (Acts 8:9, 13:6-11).

13.3.0.en: He calls them to walk in the way of the Lord and in His fear, to keep His commandments, to obey Him, to hold fast to His worship and to cleave to Him all their days.

13.4.0.en: The false prophet and dreamer who tries to lead the people astray and draw them away from God must be put to death, in order to root out evil and preserve the faith of the people.

13.4.1.en: Hold fast to your faith which you learned in the Church, however much the wicked try to make you doubt it; on the contrary, read the spiritual books that explain the faith to you and apply this faith in your life, and you will feel God and He will bless you in all your ways.

13.4.2.en: (2) The wicked relatives (vv. 6-11:) 6 "If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers; 7 Namely, of the gods of the people which are round about you, nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth; 8 Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him: 9 But thou shalt surely kill him; thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people. 10 And thou shalt stone him with stones, that he die; because he hath sought to thrust thee away from the LORD thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage. 11 And all Israel shall hear, and fear, and shall do no more any such wickedness as this is among you."

13.5.0.en: The enticement may come from a full brother, a son, a daughter, a wife or a friend dear to you, that is, from your closest relatives, calling you to worship false, pagan gods of which you have not experienced any work in your life and which had no influence on your affairs, either for you or for your fathers, gods that the other peoples worshiped in the regions around you or in the countries far from you, throughout the length and breadth of the earth. This reminds us of what happened with the wives of King Solomon when they enticed him to worship strange gods.

13.6.0.en: Do not listen to this relative who tries to draw you away from God, and do not pity him, for he will lead many astray if you leave him, and do not conceal his sin because of its gravity and his persistence in it. So after it is confirmed, he must be put to death; he is to be stoned with stones, and your hand is to be the first to cast a stone at him, and then the people, in order to root out evil, so that God may be pleased with you.

13.7.0.en: The reason for this death sentence is this relative's attempt to draw Israel away from the worship of his God, who brought him out of the slavery of Egypt. In this way he becomes a lesson to any other person who is tempted in his own mind to entice the people onto a path far from their God, and fear fills everyone's hearts.

13.7.1.en: Do not agree to evil if it comes to you from one of those close to you, and do not flatter him, but be strong in refusing evil and do not take part in it even if this relative is displeased with you, for pleasing God is more important than pleasing people. In this way you save your soul and alert this relative, perhaps he will repent.

13.7.2.en: (3) The apostasy of a city from God (vv. 12-18:) 12 "If thou shalt hear say in one of thy cities, which the LORD thy God hath given thee to dwell there, saying, 13 Certain men, the children of Belial, are gone out from among you, and have withdrawn the inhabitants of their city, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which ye have not known; 14 Then shalt thou enquire, and make search, and ask diligently; and, behold, if it be truth, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought among you; 15 Thou shalt surely smite the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, destroying it utterly, and all that is therein, and the cattle thereof, with the edge of the sword. 16 And thou shalt gather all the spoil of it into the midst of the street thereof, and shalt burn with fire the city, and all the spoil thereof every whit, for the LORD thy God: and it shall be an heap for ever; it shall not be built again. 17 And there shall cleave nought of the cursed thing to thine hand: that the LORD may turn from the fierceness of his anger, and shew thee mercy, and have compassion upon thee, and multiply thee, as he hath sworn unto thy fathers; 18 When thou shalt hearken to the voice of the LORD thy God, to keep all his commandments which I command thee this day, to do that which is right in the eyes of the LORD thy God."

13.8.0.en: Children of Belial: that is, sons of evil who lead the people of Israel astray from God.

13.8.1.en: If wicked men appear in one of the Jewish cities and lead the whole city astray from God and decide to worship one of the pagan gods, they must be punished severely.

13.9.0.en: So you must first examine the matter with all care and verify that it has really happened and that the report which came to you is true and certain, for this means that this shameful thing which does not please God has actually been done.

13.10.0.en: Destroying it utterly: you kill and wipe out everything in it and take nothing from it for yourself.

13.10.1.en: So pass sentence of destruction on the inhabitants of that city, and the whole city and all its goods are to be burned with fire, and its inhabitants and their cattle are to be destroyed, put to the sword, so that the city becomes a heap of dust and is left a ruin and is not rebuilt afterward.

13.11.0.en: The sentence of putting cities under the ban required the destruction of the city with everything in it without exception, and no one of the people of Israel was to take anything from it for himself (this reminds us of what happened with Achan the son of Carmi, who violated this commandment at the conquest of the city of Ai and took something for himself from Jericho, which was under the ban, so the people stoned him (Josh 7:35, 36). In this way the curse falls upon it, and the anger of the Lord is quenched and He grants you mercy and multiplies your number and blesses you as He swore to your fathers, as long as you keep His commands and carry them out with all exactness.

13.11.1.en: Keep away from evil places that cause you to stumble, and do not keep anything that could make you fall into sin, and know that a single evil picture that you are careless about looking at can trouble you for many days, and be sure that your relationship with God is more precious than any passing material desire.

13.11.2.en: The permitted, the forbidden and the tithes

14.0.1.en: Baldness between your eyes: shaving the eyebrows because of grief.

14.0.2.en: God was careful that His people should keep away from the pagans and not imitate them in any practices they perform to please the pagan gods. When the pagans died they would wound their bodies, and this is against respect for the body which God created; likewise they would shave their eyebrows, and this also changes the form of the human being which God created. So He required His people not to do such practices, so that they might keep their sonship to Him and enjoy His care for them.

14.1.0.en: God reminds them that they are holy and set apart for His worship and must keep away from pagan worship. They are a people special to God, distinct from the rest of the peoples and higher than they, because of their worship of God and His presence among them.

14.1.1.en: Your distinction from all those around you is in God's dwelling within you, so do not imitate the world in its evil speech and conduct, lest you anger God and hinder His work in you, and examine yourself every day to be purified from the thoughts of the world.

14.2.s.en: (2) The permitted and the forbidden among land and sea animals

14.2.0.en: To begin with, the Lord asks them to have clean food, so that the believer may always think of purity and holiness even in his eating and drinking, so he had to distinguish between permitted and forbidden foods.

14.3.0.en: The Lord specifies for them the clean animals, which are:

14.3.4.en: 4- The hart: a kind of mountain buck.

14.3.6.en: 6- The fallow deer: an animal resembling the gazelle and tending to a reddish color.

14.3.7.en: 7- The wild goat: the mountain buck.

14.3.9.en: 9- The wild ox: a kind of wild cattle.

14.4.1.en: Cheweth the cud: it keeps food in a special place in the stomach and then brings it back to the mouth to chew it. The permitted animal is distinguished from the forbidden by the following two conditions:

14.4.2.en: 1- A split hoof. 2- Chewing the cud.

14.4.3.en: This has already been mentioned in (Lev 11:3).

14.5.0.en: If the animal chews the cud but its hoof is not split, it is not eaten, such as the camel, the hare and the coney, an animal resembling the hare but without a tail, which lives in burrows. Likewise it is not eaten if its hoof is split but it does not chew the cud, such as the swine. The flesh of these animals is not eaten and their carcasses are not touched. There is more than one direct reason for the prohibition of eating some animals. Modern studies have proved that eating the flesh of some animals results in health hazards because the food of those animals is poisonous grasses; in addition, some of those animals were associated with pagan practices, some being used as sacrifices to idols such as the camel, and some being pagan symbols of certain ancient societies, so God wanted to set His people apart so that they would not share with the Gentiles in their abominations. Whatever the reasons, the application of this distinction between the clean and the unclean shows the people's obedience to God and their readiness to fulfill the requirements of the covenant with Him.

14.5.1.en: Not touching the carcasses of the forbidden animals is because they make unclean whoever touches them, and from the health standpoint they may transmit some diseases. Besides the direct reasons, there are symbolic spiritual meanings:

14.5.2.en: Chewing the cud applies to the believer, in the spiritual sense, who feeds on the living word of God when he always reads God's word and rereads it and meditates on it, as David says in his Psalms: "Blessed is the man ... in the law of the LORD doth he meditate day and night" (Ps 1:2). As for the splitting of the hoof, it means the believer who is led in his life by the spirit of discernment, so he distinguishes between what is suitable for his spiritual and eternal life and what is not beneficial, and avoids conduct in it and sets it aside. It also means the ability to bear weariness, and so signifies spiritual striving.

14.5.3.en: In Christianity, after the spiritual symbols were understood, it became permitted to eat all the animals that a person wants, as appeared in Peter's vision (Acts 10:11), because God created everything blessed and we keep away only from sin; and of foods we abstain from blood and what is strangled (Acts 15:20).

14.5.4.en: Much meditation on the word of God purifies a person, so make it a daily food for yourself on which you meditate again and again.

14.6.1.en: The standard of what is permitted among sea animals is the presence of fins and scales; what has no fins and scales is forbidden and is not eaten because it is unclean.

14.6.2.en: An example of this is the eel, since it has neither fins nor scales, so it is among the forbidden sea animals. There is a health reason for this, which is that the shelled animals feed on filth, which may cause some diseases.

14.6.3.en: The spiritual symbolic meanings of this are:

14.6.4.en: Just as fins help in swimming, so the believer in the world is surrounded by currents opposed to his spiritual course, so he must strive and not yield to the currents of evil.

14.6.5.en: As for the scales, they are a protection for fish, as the grace of God protects us in our spiritual striving.

14.6.6.en: Beware of forgetting the means of grace such as repentance, confession, Communion, prayer and reading the Holy Bible, for without them you are drawn to the current of the world and go along with it.

14.7.0.en: The Law permitted the eating of clean birds, and at the same time in the following verses it forbids the birds that are forbidden to eat, as also mentioned in (Lev 11:13-25).

14.8.0.en: The forbidden birds that He forbids them to eat are:

14.8.1.en: The eagle: a large wild bird that seizes its prey; it symbolizes theft.

14.8.2.en: The ossifrage (al-anuq): called the bearded one, it resembles the eagle and throws its victim down from a height to smash it; it symbolizes cruelty. The osprey: a coastal bird that eats fish; it symbolizes seizing.

14.8.3.en: The kite: a wild bird that lives by seizing and eating stinking carcasses and feeds on filth. The sparrowhawk: a wild bird of prey like the kite, sharp of sight. It symbolizes the use of talents for evil. The raven: a wild bird that seizes prey and loves stinking carcasses; it symbolizes theft and greed. The ostrich: a huge wild bird that does not sit on its eggs in the nest; it symbolizes recklessness and not bearing responsibility.

14.8.4.en: The male ostrich: the male of the ostrich, more beautiful than the female. It symbolizes vain outward beauty. The gull: the seagull, a sea bird that snatches; it symbolizes theft and greed.

14.8.5.en: The hawk: like the falcon, it is used in hunting and symbolizes injustice.

14.8.6.en: The owl: a wild night bird, and it symbolizes ruin because it lives in ruins.

14.8.7.en: The cormorant: a coastal bird that dives to seize fish; it symbolizes theft.

14.8.8.en: The crane: a large long-legged bird that cries out much, and it symbolizes noise and restlessness. The pelican: a strong bird of prey that loves to swim; it symbolizes ferocity.

14.8.9.en: The quq: a water bird like the swan, and it symbolizes ruin.

14.8.10.en: The vulture: a bird of prey like the eagle, and it symbolizes evil.

14.8.11.en: The stork: a bird that eats frogs and insects, with a long beak and long legs. It symbolizes uncleanness and lack of discernment.

14.8.12.en: The parrot: a predatory bird that imitates speech, and it symbolizes light-mindedness.

14.8.13.en: The hoopoe: a skillful wild bird that eats worms and insects, and it symbolizes hypocrisy and outward beauty. The bat: among the flying mammals, a bird of prey, and some kinds of it suck blood; it symbolizes parasitism.

14.8.14.en: He defines the traits of the unclean birds as being predatory, fierce in nature, and eating carrion, that is, stinking carcasses and filth, despite the beauty of their outward appearance. They point to the traits of the wicked and their hypocrisy, as mentioned in the preceding description of the birds, and they show the necessity of the purity of the source of our teaching and our spiritual food, and the necessity of gentleness and of not wronging others.

14.9.0.en: Creeping: the insects that fly and at the same time walk on the ground, that is, creep upon it.

14.9.1.en: Flying insects in general are forbidden to eat, except some that are permitted to eat, which are not mentioned here but are mentioned in (Lev 11:21, 22), namely the locust, the bald locust, the beetle and the grasshopper (all of them species of locust). We note that these insects have strong hind legs which help them to leap.

14.9.2.en: Insects in general feed on filth, so they are defiled, which points spiritually to the person immersed in defiled deeds who lives his life by eating of them.

14.9.3.en: Those with strong hind legs signify spiritually the believer who is lifted out of his falls, impelled by his longings to rise toward heavenly things.

14.9.4.en: Clinging to earthly things and constantly thinking about them defiles a person and gradually turns his thoughts to evil. So look always to heaven and take care of your prayers with the saints, and you will rise in your life above sin and above passing material things and rejoice in fellowship with God.

14.10.0.en: The death of a person takes him to Hades because of sin, since Christ had not yet accomplished redemption in the Old Testament; therefore touching carcasses defiles, and of course eating the carcasses of animals defiles, to declare the gravity of sin which led to the death of man and animal. Although the animal did not sin, it became defiled and its carcass became unclean because of man, who was defiled by sin. The prohibition of eating carcasses came also for health reasons, for eating the flesh of carcasses exposes a person to infection or poisoning; and at present the food-control laws of the state's agencies forbid the sale of the meat of carcasses. As for the matter of giving it to the stranger who dwells among them or selling it to a foreigner, it added nothing to what already existed, since the pagan peoples did not forbid the eating of carcasses, and the Law came to the people set apart for the Lord, whom He separated from among the peoples to be a holy possession, by which they rise above the abominations of the other peoples.

14.10.1.en: There is a symbolic meaning to this prohibition, which is that the Lord wants the believers to turn away from dead things and always to feed on the life-giving word of God.

14.10.2.en: As for the second part of this verse, which is the prohibition of boiling a kid in its mother's milk, which was also mentioned in (Ex 23:19), God wants to teach His people kindness to the irrational creation, for God does not want the heart of the mother (the goat) to be broken over her young one in the first period of its nursing, which the infant also needs, for the instinct of motherhood is very strong toward the young (in animals) before weaning, and it lessens gradually afterward.

14.11.s.en: (4) The tithes and the annual firstlings

14.11.1.en: The Lord commanded His people to set apart a tenth of what an individual obtains of the good things of the land, which are the wheat, the grape juice and the oil, and likewise the firstborn of the cattle and sheep he owns, as an acknowledgment by the believer that the Lord is the true owner of the land and all that is on it, and therefore what a person owns is a gift from the Lord, and the one who offers the tithes must bring them to the temple, where they are offered in the form of love feasts (agape) in which the one who offers them shares with others. In this way a person eats with his family and with the poor and thanks God.

14.12.0.en: If the dwelling place of the one who offers the tithes is far from the temple, so that it is hard for him to transport the offerings and walk with them long distances to reach the temple, he may sell them and go with their price to the temple and spend it there on buying cattle, sheep and grape juice to hold the communal feast there, in which the members of his household and the Levite who lives with him in his city share with the one who offers the tithes. The Lord stressed the necessity of not forgetting the Levite because he did not own land like the rest of the tribes. The commandment joined the holding of the feast with joy, for it is joy in the favors of the Lord, who is the giver of all these good things and has poured out His generosity and bounty on us and on those around us. And the eating of the tithes by the one who offers them together with the Levites is a showing of fellowship of love and sympathy with them and a keeping away from any haughtiness on the part of the one who offers the tithes because of what he has given. And going to the temple every year to offer the tithes is a means the Law uses to bind all the believers to the temple of God and His worship, so they offer the tithes there.

14.13.0.en: Every three years the system of distributing the tithes differs, as the third year is the share of the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless and the widow, so no one takes anything of it to the place of the temple, but it is kept in the cities where those who offer the tithes live and is devoted to meeting the needs of the groups mentioned. The Lord attaches to the commandment a promise that if it is followed, He blesses all the works that the one who offers it does, so that he has much good; by the blessing of the tenth, the other nine tenths are blessed. And his not going to the temple in the third year and distributing the tithes to the needy in his city helps him to care for the sick and the infirm who are unable to go to the temple.

14.13.1.en: Take care to offer the tithes in order to thank God for His gifts and rejoice with the needy and receive many blessings; indeed, the more your love increases, the more your gifts exceed the tithes.

14.13.2.en: The seventh year and the firstborn of the animals
